title: Consultation, e-prescriptions & pharmacy dispensing
summary: EMR notes with correction-only edits, formulary with live stock, FEFO partial dispensing, OTC, Zakat.
markdown:
# Consultation, prescriptions & pharmacy

## Clinical note

1. `POST /clinical-encounters {"ticket_id", "chief_complaint", …}` (draft) → `PATCH` while drafting. Send an
   `Idempotency-Key` (one per note, the same on a retry), so a lost answer never leaves two notes.
   **Examination consent**: before examining, the doctor asks the patient (or a parent or relative) and records
   `examination_consent`: `VerbalObtained` (printed as "VCO"), `Declined` or `NotExamined`. The last two leave the
   examination empty (`VALIDATION_ERROR`). Offer three unselected buttons, never a default. The server stamps who and
   when (`examination_consent_stamp`). Under the **Clinic** profile an OPD or follow-up note is finalized only with it
   (`EXAMINATION_CONSENT_REQUIRED`; the clinic manual, indicator 41). A hospital records it when it wishes.
   **A clinic's complete note** (the clinic manual, indicator 28: the record shows the history, the findings, the
   diagnosis and the treatment or referral): under the Clinic profile an OPD or follow-up note is also finalized only
   with the complaint (or history), the examination findings when VCO was obtained, a diagnosis and the plan.
   `CONSULTATION_INCOMPLETE` lists what is empty in `details.missing`; keep the draft and mark those fields.
2. `POST /clinical-encounters/{id}/finalize` → immutable; ticket becomes `Examined`. Diagnosis codes (`icd_codes`) come
   from the ICD picker and must be in the active code list; they come back with titles in `icd_terms`
   ([ICD coding](icd-coding.md)).
3. Later changes: `POST /clinical-encounters/{id}/correction {"reason", …}` (history kept; with an
   `Idempotency-Key` too).
4. Writes after refund/void/death are refused (`CLINICAL_LOCKOUT`) or flagged for risk review.
5. Print a finalized note: `GET /clinical-encounters/{id}/print-payload` (A4, `printer_role` document) or its
   `pdf_url` (`GET /clinical-encounters/{id}/pdf`). A draft is not printed (`ENCOUNTER_NOT_FINAL`).

### A bedside procedure note (MSDS IMS 150)

A procedure done outside the theatre (a chest drain, a central line, a lumbar puncture, suturing) is a note of type
`Procedure` on the visit or the admission, with the structured `procedure`:

1. `POST /clinical-encounters`
   ```json
   { "ticket_id": 912, "encounter_type": "Procedure",
     "procedure": { "procedure_name": "Intercostal chest drain", "site": "Right chest, 5th intercostal space",
                    "indication": "Tension pneumothorax after decompression", "anaesthesia": "Local",
                    "consent_id": 77, "assistant_employee_id": 14, "started_at": "2026-10-03T09:10:00+05:00" } }
   ```
   The consent comes from the consent register (the patient's own, see [consent](consent.md)); the assistant is picked
   with `GET /staff/lookup?q=` (the badge facts of active staff).
   The procedure's informed consent (`procedure.consent_id`) from the patient's signed consents,
   `GET /consents?patient_id=`.
2. While a draft: `PATCH /clinical-encounters/{id} {"procedure": {"technique", "findings", "specimens", "complications",
   "condition_at_end", "ended_at"}}` (only the fields sent change). `procedure.missing` lists what signing still needs.
3. `POST /clinical-encounters/{id}/finalize` signs it only with the findings, the specimens ("None" if nothing was
   removed) and the patient's condition at the end: `PROCEDURE_NOTE_INCOMPLETE` with `details.missing` otherwise. The
   provider is the note's author (its stamp). Signed, the procedure is frozen; a correction uses `"field": "procedure"`.
4. The note prints with the procedure first; the record review and the inspection pack count it.

### The author stamp (MSDS IMS 147)

Every clinical entry names its author with a **stamp**: name, designation and specialty, PMDC/PNC registration, and
the date and time, as the author's staff record stood at that moment (a later promotion or name change does not
rewrite an old printout). The same object (`name`, `designation`, `registration`, `at`, `text`) appears on screen and
on paper; print `text` under the entry:

| Where | Field |
|---|---|
| clinical note (and each correction) | `author_stamp` (who finalized it; null while a draft) |
| prescription | `prescriber_stamp` (printed above the signature line of the slip) |
| lab result | `performed_stamp` (technician) and `verified_stamp` (verifier) |
| radiology report | `reported_stamp` |
| nursing note | `author_stamp` (PNC number) |
| admission | `details_stamp` (who recorded the reason and diagnosis) |

The discharge summary and the death certificate freeze their signer's stamp when signed (`signer_*`, `certifier_*`).

## E-prescription (§3.1–§3.3)

Offer Hospital Pharmacy only while dispensing is Active (`GET /establishment`, `x-capability-gates`); otherwise offer
only the printed slip for an outside pharmacy (`destination: "ExternalMarket"`, `CAPABILITY_INACTIVE` otherwise).

* `GET /drugs/search?q=amox` → formulary with `stock_status` (`InStock` / `Low` / `OutOfStock`) — colour it
  and keep it live with `pharmacy.stock.updated`.
* `POST /prescriptions`
  ```json
  { "ticket_id": 42, "destination": "HospitalPharmacy",
    "items": [ { "drug_id": 5, "qty_prescribed": 12, "dose_text": "500 mg", "route": "Oral",
                 "frequency_code": "TDS", "duration_days": 4 } ] }
  ```
  `destination: "ExternalMarket"` names a drug of the list (`drug_id`: its high-alert, look-alike and restricted
  checks follow it, and an inpatient's dose of it is charted with them) or a free-text drug (`external_drug_name`) when
  it is not on the list, and only prints a slip
  (`GET /prescriptions/{id}/print-payload`, with the prescriber's stamp above the signature line); it never enters
  the pharmacy queue.
  The prescription is written in the consultation (its `ticket_id` and `encounter_id`) or for an inpatient (the stay's
  `admission_id`); `patient_id` follows from either.
* An **outpatient** line (an OPD or ER visit, either destination) needs `dose_text`, `route`, `frequency_code` and
  `duration_days`; a single STAT dose (`is_stat`) needs the dose and the route. Otherwise the answer is
  `PRESCRIPTION_INCOMPLETE`, and `details.lines` lists each line's missing fields. The quantity never stands in for
  the duration. Send the consultation's `encounter_id`: the printout then carries its clinical context.
* The printout (`GET /prescriptions/{id}/print-payload`) is the standard prescription of the clinic manual (indicator
  33). It carries:
  - the patient's particulars in `fields.patient`: s/o d/o w/o, age, gender, address, contact, allergies, and the
    number of the visit;
  - the consultation's complaint, findings, provisional diagnosis, weight and "VCO" in `fields.consultation`;
  - each medicine with its directions in words ("1 tablet oral twice a day for 5 days");
  - the prescriber's stamp with the PM&DC number and a signature line;
  - the letterhead of the day it was written (`fields.hospital`).

  Particulars that were not recorded print as blanks to fill by hand.
* **Handing it over** is recorded, never inferred from printing: `POST /prescriptions/{id}/handover`
  `{"handed_to": "Patient" | "Attendant", "attendant_name", "copy_kept": "Electronic" | "CarbonCopy" | "Scan",
  "document_id"}`. A scan is the signed copy uploaded to the patient's documents (`doc_type` Prescription). The
  prescription's `handovers` lists every handover. The prescriber (`prescription.create`) or the dispenser
  (`pharmacy.dispense`) records it.
  The scan is uploaded with `POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents`: its answer is the `document_id`.
* Inpatient orders (`admission_id`) need `dose_text`, `route`, `frequency_code` (or `is_prn` / `is_stat`)
  and `start_at` — the MAR is generated from them (`MEDICATION_ORDER_INVALID` otherwise).
* Medication safety ([medication safety](medication-safety.md), MSDS 52, 56, 70): each medicine carries
  `high_alert_category` (show it red), `is_restricted` and `lasa_with` ("looks like …"). Only a PMDC doctor, or a
  clinician with the Prescribing privilege, prescribes, and a restricted medicine needs RestrictedPrescribing
  (`PRESCRIBER_NOT_AUTHORIZED`). `self_administration: true` lets an inpatient take an oral, inhaled or topical
  medicine that is not high-alert themselves. A nurse writes down a verbal or telephone order with
  `POST /prescriptions/verbal`; the doctor countersigns it (`POST /prescriptions/{id}/countersign`) and answers the
  pharmacist's queries (`POST /prescription-queries/{query_id}/answer`).

## Dispensing (§3.2)

The Pharmacy Admin also has a queue-only view: `GET /prescriptions/pending`. Its `rx_queue` page and F1 help are
listed in `GET /meta/handbook?workspace=pharmacy_admin`; use only the returned tasks. Opening a prescription's detail
requires `prescription.view`, and dispensing has its own permission. Do not offer those actions to a queue-only user.

1. `GET /prescriptions/pending` (event `pharmacy.prescription.pending`), Code Red first.
2. `POST /prescriptions/{id}/dispense` with `Idempotency-Key`:
   ```json
   { "items": [ { "prescription_item_id": 9, "qty": 7 } ], "payment_mode": "Cash" }
   ```
   * Partial quantities are fine ("Dispense Now"); the prescription becomes `PartiallyDispensed` and the
     patient returns for the rest without a new prescription.
   * **Batches are chosen by the server, First-Expired-First-Out** — never ask the pharmacist.
   * OPD is cash-and-carry (`OPD_PHARMACY_CREDIT_NOT_ALLOWED`); inpatients go to the running IPD bill
     automatically; staff purchases can use `StaffPayrollDeduction` (deducted in payroll).
   * A high-alert medicine needs a second person's check: `checker_username` / `checker_password` in the body
     (`HIGH_ALERT_CHECK_REQUIRED`, MSDS 57). A recalled batch is never picked.
   * An unclear or unsafe order: raise a query instead (`POST /prescriptions/{id}/queries`); the line waits for the
     doctor's answer (`PRESCRIPTION_QUERY_OPEN`). See [medication safety](medication-safety.md).
   * The lines (`prescription_item_id`) come from the prescription, `GET /prescriptions/{prescription_id}` (`items`).
3. Receipt: `GET /dispensations/{id}/receipt-payload`; one label per medicine: `GET /dispensations/{id}/labels`
   (MSDS 61).

### Pharmacy discharge clearance

Read `GET /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge-status` with `ipd.discharge.clear_pharmacy`. Confirm `patient_name`,
`mrn` and `admission_number`, and offer clearance only when `blocked_on` is `PharmacyClearance`. The response includes
the admission `status` and the stages' status, actor and time, without the clinical admission or invoice.
Before discharge starts, `started` is false and `stages` is empty. A nonexistent admission answers `NOT_FOUND`.
Clear with `POST /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge/{stage}/clear`, stage `PharmacyClearance`.
After a lost answer, read discharge-status again: a Cleared pharmacy stage with `cleared_by_name` and `cleared_at`
confirms clearance. Never automatically repeat the write or use the broader admission read for reconciliation.

## OTC (§3.5)

`POST /otc-sales {"items": [{"barcode": "8964000100017", "qty": 10}], "method": "Cash"}` with
`Idempotency-Key`. Prescription-only drugs → `OTC_PRESCRIPTION_REQUIRED`: *"Prescription required.
Cannot sell via OTC."*

## The pharmacy's cash drawer (decisions 51)

The pharmacy's cash (dispensing with `payment_mode` Cash, an OTC sale with `method` Cash) goes into the pharmacist's
**own open shift at the Pharmacy Counter** (node `PharmacyCounter`), never into a drawer the same person has open at
another counter. Card and the other payment modes need no shift.

1. Before offering Cash: `GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine?node=PharmacyCounter`. Null means no pharmacy drawer is open:
   show Cash as unavailable with *Open your cash shift at the Pharmacy Counter* and a link to My cash shift (Card still
   works). The unfiltered `GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine` may show a shift at another counter: it does not count here.
2. My cash shift is in the Pharmacy workspace's navigation (`also_uses` of `GET /meta/workspaces`; listed by
   `GET /meta/handbook?workspace=pharmacy`). It opens the shift with the node of `GET /terminals/whoami` `cash_node`,
   as everywhere: `POST /finance/cash-shifts/open {"node": "PharmacyCounter", "opening_float": 1500}`. On a PC whose
   `cash_node` is not `PharmacyCounter`, say that this PC is not set up for pharmacy cash and that IT must map it to the
   Pharmacy Counter; never let the user pick the counter, never borrow another person's shift.
3. A refusal `SHIFT_NOT_OPEN` (nothing sold, no stock or money moved) carries `details.node` `PharmacyCounter` and
   `details.open_shift`: null when the pharmacist has no drawer open, or `{shift_id, node}` of their drawer at another
   counter ("Your drawer is open at Main Reception; the pharmacy's cash needs your Pharmacy Counter drawer").
4. The close is the same as at every counter: `POST /finance/cash-shifts/{shift_id}/close {"declared_cash"}`
   ([cash shifts](finance-and-owner.md)).

## Zakat / social welfare (§3.4)

`POST /pharmacy/charity-override-request {"prescription_id", "fund_type": "Zakat", "reason",
"approver_username", "approver_password"}` — the Zakat officer co-signs at the counter (or omit the
credentials to queue it). Then dispense with `payment_mode: "CharityZakat"` and `charity_approval_id`.
Charity is an expense, never drawer cash.
The request is for the prescription at the counter (the one opened from `GET /prescriptions/pending`).

## Back office (§3.6)

Batch intake `POST /pharmacy-admin/batches` (boxes × units per box, total cost → unit cost), supplier
invoices, `low-stock`, `near-expiry`, `profit-dashboard`, write-offs `POST /pharmacy-admin/batches/{id}/adjust`.
The medicine of a batch from `GET /drugs/search`.

**Returns to the supplier** (decisions 47): stock that goes back (expired, near expiry, recalled, damaged, excess,
wrongly supplied) is not written off but returned, so the supplier's credit reaches the accounts.

1. `POST /pharmacy-admin/batches/{batch_id}/supplier-returns {"qty": 40, "reason": "NearExpiry", "note": "Collected by
   the distributor's rider"}` (`vendor_id` defaults to the supplier of the batch's invoice; a recalled batch:
   `"reason": "Recall", "recall_id": 7`). The units leave the batch, their value at cost becomes a claim on the
   supplier, and the answer is the return with `status` Returned (`INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` beyond what is in the pharmacy).
   With reason Recall, the open recall from `GET /drug-recalls`.
2. Print the return note for the goods: `GET /pharmacy-admin/supplier-returns/{return_id}/pdf`.
3. `GET /pharmacy-admin/supplier-returns` (`status`, `vendor_id`): the returns and where each stands; the accountant
   confirms the credit note ([finance](finance-and-owner.md)).
New drugs may be flagged high-alert or restricted at once (`high_alert_category`, `is_restricted`); the lists, the
look-alike pairs, recalls and the written policy are in [medication safety](medication-safety.md).
Ward indents from head nurses arrive in `/approvals` (partial approval: `items[].qty_approved`).
